verified_against.HF: Hugging Face model card / file listing (2026-10-29)
verified_against.HFsize: Weight file sizes from Hugging Face file listings (2026-11-09)
verified_against.Paper: Peer-reviewed journal publication or preprint (DOI / arXiv / bioRxiv)

patch.label: Patch encoders
patch.blurb: Self-supervised vision encoders that turn each tile into an embedding.

vl.label: Vision–language
vl.blurb: Encode images and text in one space — zero-shot classify tiles, paint probability maps, or run toxicologic and visual-omics reasoning.

slide.label: Slide encoders
slide.blurb: Aggregate patch embeddings into one vector per slide.

vmif.label: Virtual multiplex
vmif.blurb: Predict protein marker maps (mIF / CODEX) from H&E.

st.label: Spatial transcriptomics
st.blurb: Predict spatial gene expression from H&E spots across human pan-organ (STPath) and mouse (DeepSpot-M) tissues.

seg.label: Tissue segmentation
seg.blurb: Separate tissue from background, reject artifacts, or segment multi-organ mouse anatomy (TiSAM / MegaMouse).

embed_tiles.label: Embed tiles
outputs: PCA map coloured by k-means cluster

tox_vqa.label: Toxicologic / VLM decision QA
outputs: Per-tile structured morphological decision / severity scores

models.name: UNI
models.citation: Chen et al., Towards a general-purpose foundation model for computational pathology, Nature Medicine (2024)
models.species_note: Human pretraining (Mass-100K); widely validated cross-species encoder on mouse HEST-1k & DeepSpot-M.

models.name: UNI2-h
models.citation: Chen et al., Towards a general-purpose foundation model for computational pathology (UNI2-h), Nature Medicine (2024)
models.species_note: Human pretraining (>200M tiles); top cross-species transfer backbone on rodent VIPER, HEST-1k, and TiSAM/MegaMouse.

models.name: CONCH v1.5
models.notes: Vision tower used by TITAN. Text encoder is only exposed through TITAN, so zero-shot runs at slide level (see TITAN).
models.citation: Ding et al. / Lu et al., Multimodal whole-slide foundation model for pathology (CONCH v1.5 / TITAN), Nature Medicine (2025)
models.species_note: Human vision-language pretraining; benchmarked for cross-species transfer on rodent VIPER & HEST-1k.

models.name: Virchow
models.citation: Vorontsov et al., A foundation model for clinical-grade computational pathology and rare cancers detection, Nature Medicine (2024)

models.name: Virchow2
models.notes: 2560-d = CLS token concatenated with mean of patch tokens (register tokens 1-4 skipped).
models.citation: Zimmermann et al., Virchow2: Scaling Self-Supervised Mixed Magnification Models in Pathology, arXiv:2408.00738 (2024)
models.species_note: 3.1M WSI mixed-magnification encoder (5x–40x); validated on preclinical rodent & multi-stain benchmarks.

models.name: Virchow2 (CLS only)
models.citation: Zimmermann et al., Virchow2: Scaling Self-Supervised Mixed Magnification Models in Pathology, arXiv:2408.00738 (2024)
models.species_note: CLS-token variant of Virchow2 (1280-d); mixed-magnification transfer across human and preclinical slides.

models.name: Phikon
models.citation: Filiot et al., Scaling Self-Supervised Learning for Histopathology with Masked Image Modeling, medRxiv (2023)

models.name: Phikon-v2
models.citation: Filiot et al., Phikon-v2, A large and public feature extractor for biomarker prediction, arXiv:2409.09173 (2024)
models.species_note: Ungated DINOv2 ViT-L/16 trained on PANCAN-XL; benchmarked for zero-shot/linear transfer on rodent slides.

models.name: Prov-GigaPath (tile)
models.notes: Tile encoder. Its LongNet slide encoder is listed separately under slide encoders. Also feeds STPath.
models.citation: Xu et al., A whole-slide foundation model for digital pathology from real-world data, Nature (2024)
models.species_note: 1.3B real-world tile encoder; evaluated in cross-species HEST-1k and rodent transfer studies.

models.name: Prov-GigaPath-Flash (tile)
models.citation: Usuyama et al., GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Efficient Pathology Foundation Models, arXiv:2607.18218 (2026)

models.name: H-optimus-0
models.citation: Saillard et al., H-optimus-0: An Open-Source Foundation Model for Histology, Bioptimus (2024)
models.species_note: 1.1B ViT-g/14 encoder; strong cross-species morphological representation on HEST-1k mouse/human benchmarks.

models.name: H-optimus-1
models.citation: Bioptimus Team, H-optimus-1: Next-Generation Foundation Model for Histology, Bioptimus (2025)
models.species_note: 1.1B ViT-g/14 encoder (>1M slides); top linear-probe cross-species transfer encoder on rodent VIPER & HEST-1k.

models.name: Hibou-L

models.name: Hibou-B
models.notes: Lightweight ViT-B/14 (86M) sister model to Hibou-L, co-trained on human and veterinary biopsies. Runs comfortably on CPU or small GPUs.
models.citation: Nechaev et al., Hibou: A Family of Foundational Vision Transformers for Pathology, arXiv:2406.05074 (2024)
models.species_note: Explicitly co-trained on human and veterinary pathology slides.

models.name: CTransPath (CHIEF weights)
models.notes: Runs at 10x. Patch encoder for the CHIEF slide encoder.
models.citation: Wang et al., Transformer-based unsupervised contrastive learning for histopathological image classification (CTransPath), MedIA (2023)

models.name: ResNet-50 (ImageNet)
models.notes: Not a pathology model — natural-image baseline for comparisons.
models.citation: He et al., Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition, CVPR (2016)
models.species_note: Species-agnostic ImageNet natural-image baseline.

models.name: CONCH
models.notes: Zero-shot uses projected, L2-normalised image and text embeddings scaled by the model's logit_scale (CONCH starter notebook).
models.citation: Lu et al., A visual-language foundation model for computational pathology (CONCH), Nature Medicine (2024)
models.species_note: Trained on 1.17M biomedical image-caption pairs (incl. experimental pathology figures); strong rodent zero-shot transfer.

models.name: MUSK
models.notes: Zero-shot uses with_head=True, out_norm=True, ms_aug=False (MUSK README). Logit scale not documented: portal uses 100.
models.citation: Xiang et al., A vision-language foundation model for precision oncology (MUSK), Nature (2025)

models.name: KEEP
models.notes: Knowledge-enhanced VLM (ViT-L/16 + BERT). Logit scale not documented: portal uses 100.
models.citation: Zhou et al., A Knowledge-Enhanced Pathology Vision-Language Foundation Model for Cancer Diagnosis (KEEP), arXiv:2412.13126 (2024)

models.name: PLIP
models.notes: CLIP model loaded with transformers CLIPModel. Patch size/mag for slides are portal defaults, not from the model card.
models.citation: Huang et al., A visual-language foundation model for pathology image analysis using medical Twitter (PLIP), Nature Medicine (2023)

models.name: QuiltNet-B-32
models.notes: CLIP ViT-B/32 via open_clip hf-hub. Patch size/mag for slides are portal defaults, not from the model card.
models.citation: Ikezogwo et al., Quilt-1M: One Million Image-Text Pairs for Histopathology, NeurIPS (2023)

models.name: Loki (OmiCLIP)
models.notes: Visual-omics foundation model (OmiCLIP CoCa ViT-L/14) aligning H&E histology with transcriptomic gene signatures across mouse and human tissues (2.2M paired samples).
models.citation: Chen et al., A visual-omics foundation model to bridge histopathology with spatial transcriptomics (Loki / OmiCLIP), Nature Methods (2025)
models.species_note: Trained & validated on mouse and human H&E + spatial transcriptomics (ST-bank).

models.name: TissueDecision-9B
models.notes: 9B-parameter open-weight multimodal VLM purpose-built for rodent toxicologic pathology decision-making (Open TG-GATEs & NTP rat/mouse studies). Achieves 64.9% accuracy on Harvard's VIPER rodent toxicology benchmark. Supports local transformers or an OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoint (vllm_url in config.yaml).
models.citation: TissueDecision-9B: Grounded Multimodal Reasoning for Preclinical Rodent Toxicologic Pathology, arXiv:2608.26382 (2026)
models.species_note: Purpose-trained on rat and mouse preclinical toxicology slides (Open TG-GATEs, NTP CEBS, TissueDecision-Data).

models.name: TITAN
models.notes: Zero-shot follows the TITAN demo: encode_slide_from_patch_features → zero_shot_classifier(prompts, TEMPLATES) → zero_shot.
models.citation: Ding et al., Multimodal whole-slide foundation model for pathology (TITAN), Nature Medicine (2025)
models.species_note: Whole-slide VLM over CONCH v1.5; evaluated on cross-species whole-slide zero-shot tasks (VIPER).

models.name: PRISM
models.citation: Shaikovski et al., PRISM: A Multi-Modal Generative Foundation Model for Slide-Level Histopathology, arXiv:2405.10254 (2024)

models.name: PRISM2
models.citation: Shaikovski et al., PRISM2: Unlocking Multi-Modal General Pathology AI with Clinical Dialogue, arXiv:2506.13063 (2025)

models.name: CHIEF

weights.note: Clone hms-dbmi/CHIEF and download CHIEF_pretraining.pth from the Google Drive link in its README; then set the path in TRIDENT's slide_encoder_models/load_ckpts.json.

models.citation: Wang et al., A pathology foundation model for cancer diagnosis and prognosis prediction (CHIEF), Nature (2024)

models.name: Prov-GigaPath (slide)
models.notes: LongNet slide encoder over GigaPath tile embeddings.
models.citation: Xu et al., A whole-slide foundation model for digital pathology from real-world data (Prov-GigaPath), Nature (2024)
models.species_note: LongNet slide aggregator over GigaPath tiles; applicable to large rodent & human WSIs.

models.name: Prov-GigaPath-Flash (slide)
models.citation: Usuyama et al., GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Efficient Pathology Foundation Models, arXiv:2607.18218 (2026)

models.name: MADELEINE
models.citation: Jaume et al., Multistain Pretraining for Slide Representation Learning in Pathology (MADELEINE), ECCV (2024)

models.name: FEATHER (CONCH v1.5)
models.citation: Mahmood Lab, Do Multiple Instance Learning Models Transfer? (FEATHER), ICML (2025)

models.name: FEATHER (UNI2-h)
models.citation: Mahmood Lab, Do Multiple Instance Learning Models Transfer? (FEATHER), ICML (2025)

models.name: CARE
models.citation: CARE Team, CARE: A Molecular-Guided Foundation Model with Adaptive Region Modeling for WSI Analysis, arXiv:2602.21637 (2026)

models.name: GigaTIME
models.licence: Apache-2.0 (GitHub); HF terms must be accepted
models.notes: 23-channel virtual mIF. Channel order from the official gigatime_testing notebook; ImageNet mean/std from the HF config; 512 px input run as 256 px windows; sigmoid applied to logits. TRITC and Cy5 are background channels. 20x is the portal default.
models.citation: Valanarasu et al., Multimodal AI generates virtual population for tumor microenvironment modeling (GigaTIME), Cell (2025)

models.name: GigaTIME-Flash
models.notes: Listed only. The GigaTIMEFlash class is defined inside a notebook, not an importable module, so the portal has no runner yet.
models.citation: Usuyama et al., GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Efficient Pathology Foundation Models, arXiv:2607.18218 (2026)

models.name: HEX (nolan48)
models.notes: 48-marker virtual CODEX on a MUSK backbone. Patches resized to 384 px with Inception mean/std (infer_slide_h5_nolan48.py). Slide patches use a 56 µm footprint by default — adjustable.
models.citation: Li Lab (Stanford), AI-enabled virtual spatial proteomics from histopathology for interpretable biomarker discovery (HEX), Nature Medicine (2025)

models.name: STPath
models.notes: Generative spatial-transcriptomics model over GigaPath spot embeddings. Outputs log1p expression per spot.
models.citation: Huang et al., STPath: A Generative Foundation Model for Integrating Spatial Transcriptomics and Whole Slide Images, npj Digital Medicine (2025)

models.name: DeepSpot-M (Mouse ST)
models.notes: Cross-species / Mus musculus virtual spatial transcriptomics predictor built over UNI spot embeddings. Maps mouse MGI symbols (e.g. Alb, Cyp2e1, Glul, Havcr1, Ptprc, Pecam1) across rodent H&E slides.

weights.note: Clone ratschlab/DeepSpotM and place mouse ST checkpoints per its README (set deepspotm_repo in config.yaml).

models.citation: Nonchev et al. (Rätsch Lab), DeepSpot-M: Cross-Species Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction for Mouse Histopathology, medRxiv (2026)
models.species_note: Purpose-built for Mus musculus spatial gene expression prediction from H&E.

models.name: HEST tissue segmenter
models.notes: TRIDENT default. Better on IHC and dirtier slides.
models.citation: Jaume et al., HEST-1k: A Dataset for Spatial Transcriptomics and Histology Image Analysis, NeurIPS (2024)
models.species_note: Trained on HEST-1k (Homo sapiens + Mus musculus tissues across H&E and frozen sections).

models.name: GrandQC tissue segmenter
models.notes: Fast, accurate on clean H&E. Citation requested.
models.citation: Weng et al., GrandQC: A comprehensive solution to quality control problem in digital pathology, Nature Communications (2024)
models.species_note: Species-agnostic H&E tissue segmentation & artifact quality control.

models.name: TiSAM (MegaMouse)
models.notes: Tissue Segment Anything Model trained on the MegaMouse pan-organ dataset (52 mouse tissue classes across 12 organs: brain, liver, kidney, lung, pancreas, GI, heart, reproductive). Segments multi-compartment mouse micro-anatomy.

weights.note: Clone Kiemen-Lab/tisam and download the MegaMouse checkpoint from the repository release (set tisam_repo in config.yaml).

models.citation: Kiemen Lab, TiSAM & MegaMouse: Pan-Organ Multi-Class Tissue Segmentation in Mouse Histopathology, bioRxiv (2026)
models.species_note: Trained on MegaMouse (52 mouse tissue compartments across 12 Mus musculus organs).

models.name: Otsu threshold
models.notes: CPU-only fallback; no model weights.
models.citation: Otsu, A Threshold Selection Method from Gray-Level Histograms, IEEE Trans. Syst. Man Cybern. (1979)
models.species_note: Classical intensity thresholding; works across any species.

hardware_rules.source: Portal rule of thumb, not a benchmark. Replaced by measured speed and peak GPU memory once a model has run on your server.

tiers.label: CPU OK
tiers.cpu: Runs on CPU for tiles and slides; a slide takes longer than on a GPU.

tiers.label: GPU for slides
tiers.cpu: Runs on CPU for a handful of tiles; use a GPU for whole slides.

tiers.label: GPU recommended
tiers.cpu: Very slow on CPU even for tiles; use a GPU.

tiers.label: Large GPU
tiers.cpu: Needs a GPU with more memory than its weights.

benchmarks.name: VIPER
benchmarks.scope: 25 preclinical toxicologic pathology visual QA & lesion classification tasks across Open TG-GATEs and NTP studies

benchmarks.name: HEST-1k
benchmarks.scope: 1,229 paired spatial transcriptomics + H&E whole-slide profiles (49% Mus musculus, 51% Homo sapiens)

benchmarks.name: MegaMouse
benchmarks.scope: Pan-organ mouse histology segmentation benchmark spanning 52 anatomical compartments across 12 organs

benchmarks.name: Open TG-GATEs & NTP CEBS
benchmarks.scope: Large-scale toxicogenomics and preclinical H&E liver/kidney repeat-dose compound toxicity archives (>170 compounds)

benchmarks.name: TissueDecision-Data
benchmarks.scope: Curated multimodal instruction & toxicologic decision dataset paired with rodent H&E pathology findings

benchmarks.name: THUNDER & PathoROB
benchmarks.scope: Standardized multi-center clinical benchmark and scanner/stain robustness suite for patch & slide encoders

literature_references.name: TOX-FM
literature_references.scope: Preclinical rodent toxicologic pathology ViT-L/16 pretrained on >350,000 rat & mouse WSIs (proprietary weights — benchmark reference)

literature_references.name: TRACE & ToxScribe
literature_references.scope: Slide-level multimodal foundation model for rat toxicologic pathology & automated INHAND report generation (~99k rat WSIs, proprietary weights)

literature_references.name: SlideFiLM
literature_references.scope: Feature-wise linear modulation adapting human pathology FMs to drug-induced liver injury (DILI) in preclinical rat models

literature_references.name: TRIDENT
literature_references.scope: Unified toolkit for whole-slide tissue segmentation, patching, and standardized patch/slide foundation model inference
